sources.title: Djibouti eVisa replaces point-of-entry visa
sources.publisher: National Agency for State Information Systems, Republic of Djibouti
sources.officialityEvidence: Djibouti's live e-government page establishes electronic delivery after approval, but does not publish a current Greek ordinary-passport eligibility or exemption schedule.
sources.supportingExcerpt: l'eVisa est envoyé au demandeur par courrier électronique

sources.title: Liberia - Visa on Arrival
sources.officialityEvidence: The live lis.gov.lr service identifies the Liberia Immigration Service as the authority implementing the Alien and Nationality Law. It makes the arrival route depend on whether a Liberian embassy is in the traveller's country, not Greek nationality alone.
sources.supportingExcerpt: If there is a Liberian embassy in your country, you are required to apply for your visa directly at the embassy.

sources.title: Sierra Leone eVisa terms and FAQ
sources.publisher: Sierra Leone Immigration Department eVisa service
sources.officialityEvidence: Sierra Leone Immigration Department's live slid.gov.sl page links www.evisa.sl as its 'Official Portal.' The application language describes airport or border issuance after approval, while the same service also has electronic-delivery language. It does not establish one issuance point for Greeks.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Once your visa application has been approved, you'll be issued your Visa upon arrival at the airport or border.

sources.title: Virgin Islands Laws Online: related Immigration and Passport legislation
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Government laws register identifies a 2026 Immigration and Passport Visa Exemption Order, but the accessible register entry does not directly classify a Greek ordinary passport or provide issuance timing.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Immigration and Passport Visa Exemption Order, 2026
